subject: general
question: Which of the following is NOT a subatomic particle?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Molecule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A molecule is not a subatomic particle; it is a chemical structure consisting of at least two atoms bonded together.
 
• Subatomic particles include neutrons, electrons, and protons, which are the fundamental components of an atom.
 
• Molecules are formed through chemical bonds and can consist of different atoms or identical atoms.
 
• Examples of molecules include H₂O (water), CO₂ (carbon dioxide), and O₂ (oxygen).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Neutron:**

 
 
• Neutrons are subatomic particles found in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• They have no electric charge and a mass slightly greater than that of protons.
 
• Neutrons play a key role in the stability of the nucleus.
 
 
 
• **Electron:**
 
 
• Electrons are negatively charged subatomic particles.
 
• They orbit the nucleus of an atom in various energy levels.
 
• Electrons are involved in chemical bonding and electricity conduction.
 
 
 
• **Proton:**
 
 
• Protons are positively charged subatomic particles found in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• The number of protons determines the atomic number and the element's identity.
 
• Protons have a mass approximately equal to that of neutrons.
 
 
 
• **Molecule:**
 
 
• Molecules are composed of two or more atoms chemically bonded together.
 
• They can be simple (e.g., O₂) or complex (e.g., DNA).
 
• Molecules are the smallest unit of a chemical compound that retains its chemical properties.
